column1: # The package set, and the single source of truth for it.
# BuildNugets.sh packs in this order, the release and PR workflows generate their package tables
# from it, and run-simulator-tests.sh clears the local NuGet cache for every id listed here.
# Adding a package means adding a row here and a project under src/ - nothing else has a second
# copy of the list to fall out of step with.
# Rows are in dependency order: a package's in-repo deps must already have appeared above it.
# package-id
column3: deps (SFMC-family package ids it must declare, or -)

column1: MarketingCloudSDK.Net.AppGroupSDK.iOS
MarketingCloudSDK.Net.iOS
# NOT BOUND, and why.
#   SFMCSDK                  The SFMC SDK core framework. Bound by the sibling repository
#                            SFMCSDK.Net.iOS, which this package depends on - mirroring the
#                            native package manifests (sfmc-sdk-ios ~> 4.0.1).
#   PushFeatureSDK           The modular feature frameworks of the Unified SDK generation
#   IAMFeatureSDK            (push-feature-sdk-ios, iam-feature-sdk-ios, mam-core-sdk-ios).
#   MAMCoreSDK               Salesforce's integration docs route apps through the umbrella
#                            MarketingCloudSDK, which is what this repository binds; these
#                            become packages once a consumer needs one directly.
#   AppGroupSDK (API)        The framework SHIPS from this repository as a payload-only package;
#                            its API is deliberately not projected - the repository upstream is
#                            named app-group-internal-sdk, and no integration doc names its
#                            types. The package tests assert the assembly stays empty.
